newsitem.title: USA: U.S. holiday retail sales seen lower than expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. holiday retail sales seen lower than expected.

text.p: U.S. retail sales during the holiday season were generally solid, but business at most stores probably fell short of expectations, analysts said on Monday.

"This year's sales were at the lower end of expectations for (retail) corporations," said Saul Yaari, an analyst at Piper Jaffray Inc. "Most of them wanted to post high single-digit gains. But we think it was in the four to five percent range."
In November, analyst estimates indicated an overall holiday sales gain of between five and 5.5 percent.
Dain Bosworth analyst Alan Rifkin agreed that sales were mostly good, though upper-end retailers did not fare as well.

"This was a decent Christmas," he said. "Overall sales climbed about four percent compared with a year ago. All of the retailers came back from a really poor 1995, except for the real high-end companies like Gucci and Saks."
Several leading retailers, including Wal-Mart Stores Inc, Sears, Roebuck and Co, J.C. Penney Co Inc and Dayton Hudson Corp, are expected to report sales for the holiday period within 10 days.
Christopher Vroom, a retail analyst at Alex. Brown & Sons, expects sales gains of between 3.5 percent and 4.5 percent compared with sales a year ago.

"Overall, what we're getting is not a spectacular Christmas selling season but certainly a better one than last year," said Howard Eilenberg, an analyst at Redbook Research, a unit of Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc.
"I spoke to May Department Stores Co and Federated Department Stores Inc...and their business was on plan or better for the last week," Eilenberg said.
May expected same-store sales to climb by one percent, while Federated saw December same-store sales ranging between a one percent decline and a one percent gain.
Eilenberg said May's sales were ahead of expectations for the month to date, while Federated's sales were in line with forecasts. Company officials were unavailable for comment.
Wal-Mart, the nation's largest retailer, said last week that discount and warehouse sales were at the low end of expectations for the holidays just before Christmas.

"Our sales were on plan in the days just before and after Christmas," Shauna Matthews, a Wal-Mart spokeswoman, said. "And we will probably announce a mid-single-digit comparable-sales gain for our discount and warehouse stores."
"Their pre-Christmas sales ended strongly," Redbook's Eilenberg said. "Wal-Mart was also on plan for the month of December and on plan for the combined period of November and December."

Eilenberg said that sales at J.C. Penney, the nation's fifth-largest retailer, were slightly below forecast last week. Penney officials, who earlier estimated a high-single-digit gain for December same-store sales, were unavailable for comment. Those results are expected to be released on Thursday.

Sears last week said its comparable-sales gain could wind up in the high single digits. Sears spokeswoman Jan Drummond said the company would report sales for the five-week period ending January 4 five days later.
Specialty retailers were a bright spot this season, Vroom of Alex. Brown said. He cited Petsmart Inc, Borders Group and Staples Inc as examples.
"It's a reflection of fragmentation in retailing and it's a trend I think we'll see more of as consumers transfer their spending toward other areas, like health care and savings," he said.
